analysis: Examined the following changes. ModelPrefetchCoordinator.swift (head 54-58, 108-134, 289-330) replaces the void onVerified hook with publish -> String?. A non-nil refusal now produces a terminal .failed status instead of .verified. The legacy init wraps onVerified so it returns nil, which preserves prior behavior. Coalescing, taskId ownership checks in finish (349) and shutdown handling are unchanged. This change is fail-closed: a host that refuses a build no longer reports success. ProviderLoopConfig.swift adds autopilotPendingCandidates (head 13-15, 46, 52): cached catalog builds to be verified in the background before they join the Autopilot set. It is nil without saved consent. AutopilotCommand.swift registers the Downloads subcommand and updates the discussion text: once enrolled, Autopilot may download catalog models by default. AutopilotDownloadCommands.swift adds a local CLI that writes [backend.autopilot_downloads] under withMutableConfig, with limit validation (values > 0, blank means no limit). AutopilotStatusCommand.swift reads the download ledger and live snapshot for display only. No change touches attestation, encryption, cacheSalt or authorization (TB-011, T-052, T-053, T-054). It is not shown whether builds published into the Autopilot set gain serving permission without the normal weight-hash path (T-012, T-027, A-004). ProviderLoopConfig line 11 says inventory stays separate from serving permission. Integration questions: (1) the ProviderLoop publish implementation and the background verification of pendingCandidates are not supplied. Integration should confirm that only aggregate-verified builds with coordinator-consistent weight hashes join the advertised or Autopilot sets. (2) Default-on autonomous downloads add disk-consumption availability surface for the operator (T-016). The text claims AutopilotDiskGuard keeps a reserve and that a download ledger exists, but neither implementation was supplied. (3) It is unverified whether downloads stop when consent is revoked. No concrete regression was identified in the supplied units.
